data.name: Regeria Hope Episode 1
data.detailed_description:
Regeria Hope is a whimsical courtroom visual novel in the style of an Attorney game with original characters and cases. You play as Regeria, a female lawyer who can use her powers of logic and reason to prove her clients innocent.

It’s not all that straightforward though. Sometimes, you may find compelling reasons for throwing a case, forsaking the very defendant you are sworn to protect. These decisions will affect the outcome of the case and will have a ripple effect on later episodes of the series.

The first trial has you defending a husband whose wife has been poisoned during the wedding reception. Currently you have the ability to prepare your witness, and interrupt other characters while they are speaking, but be careful, as you have a time limit to solve the case!

KEY FEATURES:

5 episodes - Choices made in early episodes affect future cases. Don't like a character? You can throw them under the bus. Just be sure you're ready to watch them hang.
New 'Witness Prep' Gameplay - Prep your witness to say whatever you want. Have them plead for mercy, or make them look like buffoons in front of the court to throw the case faster.
New 'Fact Overload' Gameplay - Connect the facts together to bombard witnesses and force them to confess! You only get one shot though, so make it count!
New 'Investigation' Gameplay - Short investigation sections which will affect the courtroom scenes. Play a board game and move Regeria to where she needs to be in time!
New 'Convince the Jury' Gameplay - Be mindful of all your actions in court! Needlessly interrupting or repeating the same action over and over will change what the jury thinks of you, and you will need to state your case to the jury at the end of each daily court session.

Featuring Music by Zack Parrish!

Featuring Sprite Art by Maesketch

Featuring Background Art by Sendo

Voice Acting by:

Rachael Messer (Regeria)
Marissa Lenti (Artemis)
Dane Doyle (Judge)
Rocky Marks (Pharrell)
DigglyCerides (Hawk)

data.short_description: As Regeria Hope, clear your clients of their crimes, or watch them hang and amass power and wealth. It's up to you.

reviews.review:
Regeria Hope Episode 1 is a courtroom visual novel that clearly takes inspiration from games like Ace Attorney, but it has enough of its own ideas to make it more than just a cheap copy. I play as Regeria Hope, a lawyer who has to defend her clients in court while trying to work out what actually happened. The first case involves a husband whose wife has been poisoned during a wedding reception, and I have to question witnesses, prepare testimony and find contradictions before the time runs out. I like the basic setup because it gets straight into the mystery without wasting too much time.

The courtroom sections are easily the strongest part for me. I have to pay attention to what witnesses are saying and decide when I have enough information to interrupt them. The witness preparation system is a nice change from simply presenting evidence over and over, because I can influence what a witness is willing to say. There is also the Fact Overload system, where I can connect facts together and use them against a witness. I like having these extra mechanics because they make the investigation feel slightly more active instead of just clicking through dialogue until the correct evidence becomes obvious.

I also like that the game gives me choices beyond simply proving someone innocent. Regeria can sometimes decide that a client is not worth defending, and those decisions can affect what happens later. That gives the story a slightly darker edge than I expected from the colourful anime presentation. There are also short investigation sections before the courtroom scenes, which give me a chance to look around and gather information. The game has voice acting as well, which adds a bit more personality to the characters and makes some of the courtroom moments more entertaining.

The biggest problem for me is the presentation. The character art is colourful and expressive, but the backgrounds and overall visual design are fairly basic. I can tell this was made on a smaller budget, and sometimes the limited animation makes the courtroom scenes feel less dramatic than they could be. The writing is also a little uneven in places. There are some funny moments and interesting characters, but some dialogue feels more awkward than natural, and the tone can jump around quite a lot. I do not think that ruins the game, but it stops the story from having the same level of polish as the games it is clearly inspired by.

The time limit is another thing I have mixed feelings about. I like the pressure because it makes the investigation feel more urgent, but it can also make some sections feel unnecessarily stressful when I am trying to understand what the game expects from me. I would rather take my time with a mystery and properly consider the evidence, so having to worry about the clock can occasionally get in the way. The first episode is also fairly short, which makes sense because this is meant to introduce the wider series rather than tell a huge standalone story.

What helps is that the game is completely free, so I do not feel like I am being asked to overlook the smaller production values for a full price experience. There are also eight Steam achievements, and the episode gives me a decent introduction to the characters and its courtroom systems before the later episodes. I think it works best as a short mystery that lets me see whether I like the mechanics without requiring a huge commitment. The fact that choices are designed to carry forward also gives the first episode a little more importance than a completely isolated demo would have.

Overall, Regeria Hope Episode 1 is a fun little courtroom adventure with some genuinely good ideas of its own. I like the witness preparation, evidence connections, investigation sections and the fact that my decisions can affect what happens later. The basic presentation, uneven writing, short length and occasional frustration with the time limit keep it from reaching the higher ratings I give to stronger visual novels, but there is still a lot to enjoy here. For a free first episode, I think it does a good job introducing its world and giving me enough interesting courtroom mechanics to make me want to see where the story goes next.

Rating: 7/10
